title: The Viewport & Mobile-First Mindset 📱
description: Understand the viewport meta tag, why mobile-first, and the power of relative units.

slides.title: Why Responsive Design? 🌍
slides.content:
# One Website, Every Device

Today, users visit websites from phones, tablets, laptops, desktops, even watches. A responsive site adapts its layout, images, and interactions to the screen size and capabilities.

Without responsive design, you'd need separate websites for each device – expensive and inconsistent. Responsive web design (RWD) uses CSS to deliver an optimal viewing experience across all devices.

slides.title: The Viewport Meta Tag 🏷️
slides.content:
# Tell the Browser How to Size the Page

Mobile browsers assume a wide desktop viewport by default (usually 980px) and then scale the page down. This breaks layouts. You must include this tag in `<head>`:

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
```
- `width=device-width` – matches the screen’s width in CSS pixels.
- `initial-scale=1.0` – sets the initial zoom to 100%.

Without it, media queries won't work on mobile.

quizData.question: What happens if you omit the viewport meta tag on a mobile device?

options.text: The page will look perfect on mobile
The browser renders at a wide viewport (like 980px) and scales it down

quizData.explanation: Without the viewport meta, mobile browsers assume a desktop viewport width and zoom out, making text tiny.

slides.title: Mobile-First Design Strategy 📲
slides.content:
# Start Small, Then Enhance

Mobile‑first means designing for the smallest screen first, then adding more complex layouts as the viewport grows using `min-width` media queries.

Benefits:
- Focuses on essential content and performance.
- Avoids undoing desktop styles for mobile.
- Naturally leads to fluid, resilient layouts.

Example: start with a single‑column layout, then at `768px` switch to a two‑column grid.

slides.title: A Mobile-First Base
Relative Units: The Glue of RWD 🧪
slides.content:
# Pixels Aren't Always Best

- `%` – relative to parent container.
- `em` – relative to parent font size.
- `rem` – relative to root font size (usually `<html>`).
- `vw` / `vh` – 1% of viewport width/height.
- `vmin` / `vmax` – min or max of vw/vh.

Use `%` for widths of containers, `rem` for typography and spacing, `vw`/`vh` for full‑screen sections. They scale naturally.

quizData.question: In a mobile‑first approach, you use `max-width` media queries to add desktop styles.
quizData.explanation: Mobile‑first uses `min-width` to add styles as the screen gets larger. `max-width` is for desktop‑first (starting with desktop styles and overriding for smaller screens).
